messages:
sam: heads-up - seeing a perf regression on decode batches when functions return structured payloads. throughput drops ~12% and tail latency spikes on p50->p99.

tara: can you paste a short profile or the flamegraph?

sam: attaching quick summary: kernel-switches jump when stop-token is hit mid-batch and we do a tool handoff. kv-cache pinning also looks noisy.

javier: this sounds like two things: (1) stop-token detection forcing early per-request finalization, (2) handoff path doing synchronous kernel swap + cache flush.

anika: +1. I bet our batch formation window is too aggressive for tool-heavy workloads. If many requests emit structured tool calls, the queue ends up with lots of short-lived items and we can't assemble steady long batches.

sam: repro script inc: calls that produce JSON tool outputs and then immediate function invoke. Average seq len 64 -> 10ms decode per token. We see continuous-batcher closing batch early ~40% more often.

leo: quick config I want to try: increase hold-window to 12ms for sessions with toolcall probability > 0.5, and enable soft-preempt (allow 1 token tail before preempt). config snippet:```json
{"continuous_batcher": {"hold_window_ms": 12, "soft_preempt_tokens": 1, "toolcall_heuristic": "hold_for_kv"}}
```

javier: also add pinning hint for KV entries used across tool handoffs so kernel swap doesn't relookup hot KV repeatedly. maybe a lightweight pin TTL 500ms.

anika: curious if stop-token detection could be deferred until after the batch completes a micro-chunk to avoid tearing the batch. risk: slightly delayed tool invocation. tradeoff worth measuring.

sam: ran quick perf with hold_window 12 + soft_preempt 1 + kv_pin 500ms. p95 latency down 8%, throughput back half the gap. but we still see kernel-swap spikes on some model variants.

tara: which kernels are swapping? we should correlate with sequence length vs kernel selection thresholds. maybe tool outputs make the runtime think shorter sequences are dominant -> different attention kernel chosen mid-batch.

sam: exactly. profile shows frequent kernel selection changes after tool handoff - the runtime picks a shorter-seq optimized kernel for the rest of the batch which triggers extra memcpy and kernel-launch overhead.

javier: proposal: delay kernel re-selection until batch finish or next batch start unless the majority of active streams cross threshold. or run hybrid kernel that handles both short/long with a small perf tax.

leo: I'll prototype a threshold hysteresis (require >60% of streams to change window for reselect) + kv-pin. can we run A/B on canary cluster?

infra-bot: scheduled canary job 1976543210-canary-1 for eng-runtime at 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z (config: hold_window_ms=12, soft_preempt_tokens=1, kv_pin_ms=500, kernel_hysteresis_pct=60).

anika: thanks. Also let's capture more granular stop-token timing: at-detect vs at-finalize. Add a flag report_stop_detection_timing=true to telemetry.

sam: noted. I'll collect the telemetry and a small prompt set for regression checks. if canary looks good we'll roll to dedicated and adjust defaults for tool-heavy routes.

tara: one more: update docs/arch note about toolcalls increasing batch churn and include recommended config knobs for customers (hold_window, soft_preempt, kv_pin). short blurb enough.

sam: yep will draft. thanks all :thumbsup:
